issues: Severe node ID format inconsistency: 6+ incompatible formats coexist (e.g., `class:SimpleName`, `class:SimpleName::path`, `class:path#SimpleName`, `function:method`, `function:method::path`, `function:path#method:line`). This is the root cause of most edge loss — edges from one batch reference IDs that don't exist in other batches.
Batch 17 uses a completely distinct ID scheme (`class:path#ClassName`, `function:path#method:line`) that cannot match any other batch, causing all its cross-batch edges to drop.
196 nodes have empty summaries and empty tags — all are function/method nodes from batches with the `function:path#method:line` format (primarily batch 9 and batch 17).

8 duplicate class entries exist (e.g., `class:StIf` appears as both a simple ID from the Rust grammar and as `class:src/.../StIf.java:StIf` from the Java grammar). The merge script merged by exact ID match, so the same real-world class in different subprojects became separate nodes.

12 overload groups where the same method name appears as separate function nodes with appended line-number suffixes (e.g., `visit:259`, `visit:265`, ...) instead of being modeled as a single overloaded function with multiple signatures.
132 file nodes lack a `language` field, making type-based filtering unreliable. Only the earliest file nodes (batches 1-2) have `language: 'java'` set.
`type: 'file:java'` used for 23 nodes — the subtype leaked into the type field instead of being a separate property, likely a batch-generation bug.
79 simple classes (<= 2 methods) are incorrectly marked `complexity: 'moderate'` when they should be `complexity: 'simple'`.
18 edges use type `'import'` (singular) vs 530 using `'imports'` (plural) — typo inconsistency.
Config files use inconsistent type values: some `'type': 'config'`, some `'type': 'node'` with `id: 'config:...'`
18 nodes have type `'code'` which is a flat code-blob extraction without file/class/function decomposition. These nodes lack proper summaries, tags, and structure.
warnings: Only 129 edges (13.6%) cross module boundaries (e.g., autumn→utils, rust→uranium). The graph is heavily intra-module, meaning the understanding of how modules depend on each other is weak.
The importMap recovery added 269 edges, but many more import relationships were likely lost due to ID format mismatches. The actual number of imports across batches is likely 500+.
Node density is low: 990 nodes / 950 edges = ~1 edge per node. A well-connected codebase graph should have 2-3 edges per node for meaningful analysis.
Several file nodes lack `sizeLines`, `startLine`, `endLine`, or `methodCount` fields that other file nodes have, making analytics unreliable.
Function nodes in the `function:simple` format (236 nodes) have no line number info, no params, and no complexity assessment beyond 'moderate'.
recommendations: Normalize all node IDs to a single canonical format: `type:path#name` (e.g., `class:src/norswap/lang/rust/ast/Node.java#Node`, `function:src/norswap/lang/rust/ast/Node.java#hashCode`). Apply this retroactively to all batches before merge.
Deduplicate nodes after ID normalization: merge the 8+ duplicate class entries and 12+ overloaded function groups into single nodes with metadata arrays.
Add a re-run of import edge generation after ID normalization. Currently ~530 import edges exist; after ID alignment this should rise to 800+.
Fill missing summaries and tags for the 196 empty nodes — use a batch LLM call keyed on filePath and function signature.
Add `language: 'java'` to all 132 file nodes missing the field. Add `sizeLines`, `methodCount` to all file nodes where missing.
Drop or convert the 18 `type: 'code'` nodes into proper file + class nodes, or tag them clearly as 'incomplete-extraction'.
Re-evaluate complexity on all 79 simple classes tagged as 'moderate' — use methodCount + SLOC heuristics.
Consider adding `calls`, `extends`, `implements`, and `memberOf` edge types currently missing from the graph. The only structural edges are `contains` and `imports`.
Fix the batch generation pipeline to emit a consistent `type` field for config files (all `'type': 'config'`).
